 Hurricane Vance to rapidly intensify into major hurricane, while Typhoon Champi threatens Taiwan and Japan
 Monster Typhoon Champi still has sustained winds of 120 mph after tying Super Typhoon Sinlaku earlier this week as the strongest storm to form in any basin this year.
 By
 Angela Fortuna , Julian Atienza 
 Source

 Facebook

 Copy Link
 04:46 Hurricane Vance to rapidly intensify into major storm, while Champi threatens Taiwan and Japan 
 Vance strengthened into a hurricane early Friday, becoming the 13th hurricane in the Pacific Basin this season as it approaches Mexico next week. Hurricane Vance is now forecast to rapidly intensify into a major hurricane by Friday night, which would be the basin's 10th Category 3 or stronger storm this year. Meanwhile, monster Typhoon Champi still has sustained winds of 120 mph after tying Super Typhoon Sinlaku earlier this week as the strongest storm to form in any basin in 2026. 
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 Vance strengthened into a hurricane early Friday, becoming the 13th hurricane in the Pacific Basin this season.
 Vance becomes the first V-named storm in the eastern Pacific since 2018.
 Earlier this week, Champi in the western Pacific tied Super Typhoon Sinlaku as the strongest storm on Earth in 2026.
 Vance strengthened into a hurricane early Friday, becoming the 13th hurricane in the Pacific Basin this season as it approaches Mexico next week. Hurricane Vance is now forecast to rapidly intensify into a major hurricane by Friday night, which would be the basin's 10th Category 3 or stronger storm this year.
 Meanwhile, monster Typhoon Champi still has sustained winds of 120 mph after tying Super Typhoon Sinlaku earlier this week as the strongest storm to form in any basin this year. 
 WHAT’S THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A TROPICAL DEPRESSION, TROPICAL STORM AND HURRICANE? 
 Hurricane Vance stats.
 (FOX Weather) 
  Vance was named south of Mexico on Wednesday, becoming the first V-named storm in the basin since 2018, as conditions remained favorable for tropical development across the region.
 One factor that could help Vance continue to organize is a strong Tehuantepecer wind event along southern Mexico. These powerful offshore winds force cooler air through the Chivela Pass, a gap in the mountains of southern Mexico. 
 SUPER EL NIÑO FUELED WINTER COULD UNLEASH MORE STORMS, DRIVING MORE ACTIVE PATTERN INTO THE SOUTH 
 Tehuantepecer winds explainer.
 (FOX Weather) 
  As those winds push offshore, they can interact with the surrounding tropical environment and increase the amount of spin in the lower atmosphere . When that spin lines up with an existing tropical disturbance and warm ocean waters, it can help thunderstorms organize around a developing area of low pressure.
 'EVOLVING CRISIS': COULD EL NIÑO BRING NEEDED RAIN TO THE 2 LARGEST RESERVOIRS IN THE US? 
 Forecast models have suggested Vance could initially move northwest before turning somewhat back toward Mexico. The FOX Forecast Center will continue to monitor for changes in strength and track.
 Hurricane Vance forecast cone.
 (FOX Weather) 
  Super Typhoon Champi 
 Meanwhile, Super Typhoon Champi remains an exceptionally powerful storm in the western Pacific after rapidly intensifying to maximum sustained winds of 185 mph with gusts to 225 mph.
 At that intensity, Champi tied Super Typhoon Sinlaku as the strongest storm on Earth in 2026.
 NASA SATELLITES REVEAL STRIKING OCEAN COLOR CHANGE AS SUPER EL NIÑO STRENGTHENS 
 Super Typhoon Champi stats.
 (FOX Weather) 
  Champi intensified over extremely warm waters with little wind shear and limited dry air nearby, providing an ideal environment for the storm to strengthen.
 COULD HISTORY REPEAT ITSELF? HOW PAST SUPER EL NIÑO WINTERS OFFER CLUES ABOUT WHAT'S AHEAD 
 The typhoon has also generated enormous seas. Significant wave heights near the storm's center reached 68 feet, representing the average height of the highest one-third of waves.
 Strongest storms on Earth.
 (FOX Weather) 
  Champi is expected to gradually weaken as it makes a close approach to Taiwan before likely curving toward Japan.
 HOW TO WATCH FOX WEATHER 
 A strong El Niño climate pattern has supercharged tropical development across the Pacific, with a Super El Niño expected to be declared later this year .
 Stay with FOX Weather for the latest in the tropics.
